versions.changelog: Help tab: delete one cached file (trash can column) or all HwProbe data (reports, performance results, settings history, and cache). The diagnostics zip includes HwProbe's lines from Jellyfin's log. Progress bars count only clips that aren't cached. Test suites reuse earlier measurements, with the same Earlier results choice as single runs. Shutting the server down cancels a running probe or performance test without waiting.

Recommended Settings advise software (None), first in the list and alone when no hardware works: HEVC and AV1 encoding off, BWDIF deinterlacing and key-frame trickplay from new software tests, and Allow subtitle extraction on the fly on, which is now advised for every backend so text subtitles aren't burned in (#55). Test suites copy the audio so only video is measured, except the VBR audio suite (#56).
Probes and performance tests show the shared loading bar, counting the test videos made before the tests, so the bar moves while they are made (#53).
Fixes probes failing with "Object reference not set to an instance of an object" on Intel servers. Probes show the same progress bar as performance tests.

Power draw: NVIDIA and CPU package energy where readable, shown as watts above idle, and counted in efficiency suggestions. Intel low power is tested at the bitrate Jellyfin uses, and reported as having no effect where the GPU drops it. Performance tests decode in software where the probe found decoding fails. Only the best better-quality setting is suggested, and NVENC's session limit shows as a capped stream count. The Resource Usage view shows only what was measured.

More test suites on real video: decoding, subtitle burn-in, deinterlacing (real 576i), VBR audio, legacy formats, and tone mapping by method. Legacy inputs: MPEG-2, Theora, Xvid AVI, Flash video, RealVideo, and WMV. Suggestions weigh CPU, memory, and GPU use, report the server's setting when it wins, guard concurrent streams, and can set an Internet streaming bitrate limit. Progress shows a bar with elapsed time. Fixes: HDR10 test clips are tagged correctly, and double-rate deinterlacing is measured against the field rate.

Test suites: encoder presets, quality ladder, tone mapping, thread count, Intel low power, and extras, run from Performance Tests and compared side by side in Test Results. QSV is preferred over VAAPI on the same Intel GPU. Low-power encoders that fall back to normal mode are noted, and missing ones skipped. Windows GPU usage no longer adds two decoders past 100%.
The hardware report form is cleaner and opens with the OS, versions, and working backends filled in from the latest probe. Links come from the catalog.
The page uses the window's full width, at least the dashboard's 54em, so tables with several backends have room.

Resource usage (optional, off by default): CPU, memory, GPU, and GPU memory for each measurement, in a new Resource Usage view on Test Results. Per transcode on Windows and on Linux with Intel or AMD (kernel 5.19+); whole-GPU figures for NVIDIA on Linux; CPU and memory only on macOS. Full-width cache and suggestions tables.
Third-party notices link each library's source repository.
Third-party notices: the Help tab lists the plugin's libraries with links to their licences, and every download carries LICENSE and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md.

Page polish: status icons, sortable full-width tables, collapsible sections, progress with time remaining, results hidden while a probe runs. Performance tests: live action samples at 1080p, 4K, and 8K; 3D animation 4K HDR (AV1 10-bit); per-test durations; concurrent streams must hold real time from the first frame. Same results whatever the server's or host's language.
The plugin is shown as HwProbe again. Performance Tests lists what Encoding preset Auto becomes for each backend that works on the server.

Performance tests can reuse earlier measurements with the same settings, measure the tone mapping and stereo downmix settings, and pause while the server transcodes for a player, repeating the interrupted measurement. Test Results suggests a faster hardware backend, flags outputs that fall behind real time, and suggests settings worth changing from saved runs, with Apply and Revert.

Shown as Transcoding Diagnostics. The page has five tabs: Hardware Probe, Recommended Settings, Performance Tests, Test Results and Help. Results can be shown as bars, values or a share of the fastest, and saved runs can be deleted. Help lists the cached test clips; clips no longer used are deleted automatically. Banners and buttons match the dashboard.
Probes and performance tests are no longer refused while a client is direct streaming (remux); only re-encoding video or audio blocks them.
Removes the hardware probe scheduled task (probing runs from the plugin page). The command-line tool's macOS and Linux builds now unpack as a runnable hwprobe. Simpler README.

Speed tab: measures transcode speed per working backend and software, for chosen inputs (test videos, film samples or a library file), codecs and player qualities, with Jellyfin's transcoding settings overridable for the run. Pause, cancel, history and a page styled like the dashboard.

Adds a diagnostics zip of the report and every ffmpeg log, downloaded from the plugin page or written by the command line with --diagnostics, to attach to a hardware report issue. Warns when Jellyfin is set to a backend that didn't work, and offers switching to software.

Tests QSV on every Intel adapter and AMF on the first AMD adapter on Windows, as Jellyfin picks them. Adds a Windows ARM64 command-line build. No longer guesses which GPU maker an unavailable option needs.
NVIDIA shows its pipeline tier (Full GPU pipeline (CUDA)). The plugin page fits phone screens.
Last change is one expandable line, listing what Revert sets each option to.
Shows what Revert would change. Asks to reload an open page after HwProbe is updated. HwProbe's API responses are no longer cached.
V4L2 says ARM devices only on x86. Results from an older HwProbe or a different ffmpeg are no longer shown; run the probe again after either changes.
Says when a backend needs another platform or GPU vendor. Only offers the HuC firmware fix to GPUs that have the encoder. Results link to their fix. Consistent fix wording.

Advice for trickplay (hardware decoding, MJPEG encoding, key frames only), enhanced NVDEC and BWDIF deinterlacing. Says when Jellyfin, not the GPU, uses software. Tests HEVC RExt in both 4:2:2 and 4:4:4. NVIDIA and V4L2 checked on real hardware.
A probe no longer starts during playback just after a client logs in again. The scheduled task no longer fails when the server is busy.
HwProbe in the dashboard sidebar. Plugin icon and catalog image.
Clearer documentation and plugin descriptions.
Says when Jellyfin can't open the GPU because of permissions, and how to fix it.
Restart button after switching backend. Test clips are downloaded or retried when they can't be made.
Apply and revert settings from the plugin page.
Reproducible builds.
First release.

name: HwProbe
description: Runs short test transcodes for each hardware acceleration backend and setting on the Transcoding and Trickplay pages. Shows which ones work, how to fix the ones that don't, and measures the performance of each. Recommended settings can be applied to Jellyfin's settings and reverted, or downloaded as a diagnostics zip to attach to an issue.
overview: Tests which hardware transcoding backends work on a Jellyfin server, and how fast each one transcodes
